title: Tara at the palace door
hook: a bowstring shakes the city, and Tara, one of five women Hindus remember
carry: panchakanya: Tara, the wise one, remembered daily

segments.voice: Yesterday: Lakshmana's warning went down the mountain, from a Rama who was angry but remembered the friend.
screen: `THE PATH VALI TOOK IS NOT CLOSED.`

segments.voice: The monkeys at the gates of Kishkindha see Lakshmana coming and panic. He looks, Valmiki says, like the fire at the end of the world. They scramble up walls and into trees. Some grab boulders and branches, as if that would help. Young Angada goes to meet him and is sent running back inside with the message. Lakshmana walks straight through the city, past the fine houses and gardens, and at the palace he twangs his bowstring so loudly that the whole city shakes.
screen: `PANIC AT THE GATES.` → `LIKE THE FIRE AT THE END OF THE WORLD.` → `A BOWSTRING SHAKES THE CITY.`

segments.voice: Inside, Sugriva hears the bowstring, and the party is over. He's frightened, and at first can't think what he's done wrong; Hanuman has to tell him he let the time slip. He doesn't go out himself. He sends Tara. Not long ago she was a widow grieving before Rama. Now she walks out to meet his furious brother with complete poise. Why are you angry, prince? Sugriva has been careless, yes. Even great sages have been carried away, she says, and she names Vishvamitra, who spent years with the celestial dancer Ghritachi and thought it was a single day. Then she tells him what his anger was missing: orders have already gone out. Armies are on their way. Come in. Talk to him. Lakshmana listens, and his anger cools. Hindus have a way of remembering her. A traditional morning verse names five women, the panchakanya: Ahalya, Draupadi, Sita, in some versions Kunti, Tara and Mandodari, and says that remembering them each day washes away even great wrongs. Each has a hard story. Each lived through what the world would call ruin. And the tradition puts their names on the lips every morning. Many teachers read it as honoring wisdom and strength that outlast suffering. Tara is the one remembered for counsel. She warned Vali, and he didn't listen. This time somebody listens. It meets a life now: before your anger lands, there's often news you haven't heard. And the one who brings it may be the one who's been through the most.
screen: `SUGRIVA SENDS TARA.` · `YES, HE WAS CARELESS.` · `THE ARMIES ARE ALREADY COMING.` · `THE PANCHAKANYA: FIVE WOMEN REMEMBERED.` · then, large: `THIS TIME SOMEBODY LISTENS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a woman whose wisdom came through hard things: a grandmother, a teacher, an aunt, a friend. Breathe in and say her name silently, the way the morning verse says Tara's. Breathe out and thank her for one thing she taught you. If you pray, hold her name inside your prayer; if not, simply remember her.
Lakshmana's warning. Delivered with a bowstring, and met by Tara, with the news his anger was missing.
Your line: panchakanya: Tara, the wise one, remembered daily. Her calm turned a bowstring into a conversation. Day five hundred ninety-two, done.

howItsDone: A traditional morning verse names five women, the panchakanya (Ahalya, Draupadi, Sita or Kunti, Tara and Mandodari), to be remembered daily; storytellers point to Tara here as a model of wise counsel.

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering and differ between editions; confirm against the edition the Keeper uses.
Angada going out to meet Lakshmana and returning with the message: confirm in Kishkindha 31.
Tara's example of Vishvamitra and Ghritachi (years taken for a day): paraphrased; confirm.
The text describes Tara as somewhat unsteady from drink when she goes out; the script omits this detail.
Tara's earlier words to Rama after Vali's death (Kishkindha 24) mix grief and reproach; the script now says 'grieving before Rama' rather than 'raging'. Confirm tone.
